note: Every acceptance criterion and NFR in this Unit's upstream set, mapped to the file that implements or enforces it. Targets are workspace-relative paths so the mapping is checkable mechanically; `rationale` carries what the path alone does not say. DEFERRED rows are boundaries, not gaps: U3 creates Owner and Enrollment EMPTY and never writes them [BR6.1], so every criterion needing a batch, an enrollment, a fee or a profile screen names the Unit that owns it. Where a control was verified against the WRONG implementation it exists to catch, the rationale records which tests fired and which did NOT — that distinction is the evidence, because every defect listed passes a confirmatory test.

coverage.rationale: Computed from Owner and Enrollment on every request. No role column, and no module-level cache -- the scan was verified to detect a dict, an lru_cache and a set.
Ownership gained mid-session grants the teacher lens on the NEXT request. Verified to FAIL against an injected cross-request cache; that is its only job.
The mirror, and the more dangerous direction: it GRANTS access someone should not have. Also verified against the cache.
One request one query, two requests two queries. The pair is what makes it a boundary rather than a cache.
Datastore-backed counters under a unique constraint. The two-worker test was verified to fail against a per-process dictionary.
3/hour and 5/day per number, 10/hour per IP prefix, checked BEFORE the gateway call. A breach is a ConflictError, asserted not to be a TransientError.
Expiry, single use via consumed_at under FOR UPDATE in the checking transaction, and an attempt ceiling that KILLS the code rather than only refusing the attempt.
HMAC under a server key. The not-reproducible-without-the-key test fails against bare SHA-256 while 'stored != transmitted' PASSES -- which is why both halves are stated.
Narrowest-first, with a refused scope releasing its own increment. Both accounting tests were verified to fail against global-first while every threshold test passed.
A temporary-unavailability message_key that names no limit and never says 'invalid'.

Both branches issue the SAME STATEMENTS; the unknown branch writes inside a savepoint and rolls back. Verified against both defect shapes, including the one that hashes on both branches but writes on only one.
Two name columns, two tables, two writers, asserted in both directions.
RLS ENABLED and FORCED on profile. FORCE matters independently: without it the policy does not apply to the table owner, who runs the migration.
The meta-test runs first, by collection order and a package gate. Verified: a superuser connection reads the profile even with a CORRECT policy.
Reuse invalidates the FAMILY. Against an implementation invalidating only the presented token, exactly one of five transitions fails.
Hashed refresh tokens through the same chokepoint; expiry compared against our own clock rather than the library default.
kid with two valid verification keys, tested by signing under one and verifying after the active key changed.
response_code == 202 and nothing else. A body carrying only `code` does NOT read as success -- that is the parsing the most-installed client uses.
The scheme asserted at CONSTRUCTION, with no TLS toggle exposed, asserted by signature.
One attempt, no retry. A timeout is UNKNOWN, and no code maps to TransientError across the whole table.
The null adapter is the DEFAULT; a misspelt setting yields it, and a partially configured real adapter refuses to start rather than falling back.
GSM-7 SEPTET counting: the extended set costs two, so a naive len() passes on a body needing two segments. The app hash is counted.
Owner and Enrollment created empty and never written, asserted over this Unit's AST because the violation WORKS.
No free-form column but correlation_id. The gateway's error_message is never logged, verified against an injected debug log that leaked the API key.
A committed script with a __main__ guard, never imported by application code, asserted by an AST walk over every module.
Issue returns a contentless acknowledgement for any number; the test captures the rendered SMS body at the gateway seam, which is the one place the code exists in the clear.

test_the_full_sign_in_path_returns_a_working_token_pair: issue, verify within the window, a working pair. The TEACHER LENS half needs an Owner row that BR6.1 forbids U3 from creating; the seed script supplies it at the checkpoint.
A code at 5m01s is refused; one inside the window verifies. Expiry is compared server-side.
The 6th attempt is refused AND the code is dead afterwards, so a correct 7th also fails. An implementation that counts without invalidating passes only the first half.
A timeout is UNKNOWN, never FAILED, and the user path is 'request a new code' presented as delivery failure. There is no delivery report to consult, verified against nine probed endpoints.
The number is a request-body field with no device-side source. No SMS read permission, asserted by parsing uses-permission elements and verified to fire on a real declaration.
activated_at is set via coalesce on first successful verify, so a student or guardian claims a teacher-created record without being invited.
An account with both an Owner row and an Enrollment is offered both lenses.
A student-only account gets no guardian lens -- which holds FOR FREE rather than by a check, because the guardian subquery simply returns nothing.
The switcher sends a hint in a header and decides nothing; no re-authentication is involved. The server resolves the lens from data regardless.
U3 creates the Profile table and its RLS policy; the screen that writes a self-name and photo belongs to the Unit that owns profile editing. The STORAGE and the boundary are here; the UI is not.

A teacher reads Enrollment.display_name successfully and reaches Profile by no route -- direct query, join, or ORM traversal. The two names are deliberately different so a test cannot pass by reading the wrong table.
Helper text on a screen this Unit does not build.
U3 creates Enrollment EMPTY and never writes it [BR6.1]. The existing-teacher warning is part of creating an enrollment, which is U4's.
Same boundary. U3 proves the lens RESOLVES from such a row; creating it is U4's.
Deliberately deferred so both deletion paths are specified once against the FULL schema. U3 contributes the per-table dispositions that deletion will execute.
The teacher-record-versus-child-data tension. U3 records it in the enrollment disposition rather than resolving it early.
Idempotent second deletion.
The 4th within an hour and the 6th within a day are refused, each asserting WHICH scope refused so the cascade order is actually tested.
The 11th from one IP prefix, spread across distinct numbers so the per-number ceiling is not what refuses.
Counter ROWS under a unique constraint with an atomic upsert. The two-worker test was verified to FAIL against a per-process dictionary, which is the requirement this AC states.
The global ceiling refuses and the alert fires. The counter is driven to its threshold directly because the VALUE is a deployment decision and the MECHANISM is what this Bolt builds.
A temporary-unavailability message_key. Tests assert the refusal never says 'invalid' and never names the limit.
The stored value differs from the transmitted one AND is not reproducible without the key. The first half alone PASSES against bare SHA-256, which is why both are asserted.
Byte-identical responses asserted at the HTTP boundary, and both branches issue the SAME STATEMENTS -- the write is the larger asymmetry, and a hash-only test would have left it open.
Computed per request from Owner and Enrollment. No role column exists; no module-level cache exists, asserted by a scan verified to detect a dict, an lru_cache and a set.
Teacher lens on the NEXT request after gaining ownership. Verified to fail against an injected cross-request cache.
Student lens gone on the NEXT request after losing the last enrollment -- the direction that GRANTS access someone should not have.
One request, one query; two requests, two queries. The memo lives on request.state, asserted by location rather than by intent.
Western numerals in the Bangla bundle, verified to fire on a single Bangla-Indic digit.
Server-side collation needs a list of people to order. U3 has no such list.

OTP entry is one of the named screens, and it ships with realistic Bangla rather than placeholders -- a short placeholder would hide the layout pressure the bundle exists to apply. The screenshot verifier arrives with the composables.
U3 accepts no user prose: a phone number and a six-digit code are both numeric.
Bengali-digit normalisation on a numeric field. No money or amount field crosses U3's surface.
Transaction IDs are a payment concern.
The IDOR probe needs a batch endpoint to probe. U3 builds the LENS the probe would defeat, and the route-enumeration gate that makes the endpoint impossible to add unlensed.
Same: the probe needs the endpoint.
Same.

Every refusal in this Unit carries retryable: false and one code for every cause. The OTP path returns OTP_NOT_VALID whether the code was wrong, expired or dead; the token path returns one code for unknown, expired and replayed.
The schema-wide invariant U2 built, now running against four real routes rather than an empty app. It iterates the generated document, so an endpoint added later is covered.
The hint travels out only; the client cannot grant itself a lens by asking. The server resolves from data, and resolve.py reads no hint at all.
Three of the five PUBLIC_ROUTES and the one LENS_EXEMPT_AUTHENTICATED route are opened here, and the gate passes against the real app object.
Needs data resolvable under two lenses. U3 ships the mechanism this depends on: no lens claim in the token, and a memo that dies with the request.
U2's deferred obligation: NFR14.4's equivalent-work requirement, discharged here as statement equivalence rather than hash symmetry.
ONE statement carrying three booleans and both scoping ids. My first draft used follow-up selects; the query-count assertion caught it.
ix_owner_account_id and ix_enrollment_account_id, created with the tables.
A query COUNT, never a duration: a flaky duration assertion gets deleted and takes the real check with it.
Connectivity and the applied Alembic revision, deliberately thin because the route is public and every field is disclosure.
Scheduling deploys outside classroom hours is a deployment-time decision, not code.
The verified pg_dump belongs with the deploy pipeline.
The memo on request.state, garbage-collected with the request. The LOCATION is the control.
The smoke set's endpoint exists and reports what the smoke set reads.
Image tagging and rollback.
Alembic runs as a distinct step with no URL committed, never as a side effect of application start -- the app never calls upgrade().
GLOBAL_DAILY is read from the environment rather than hardcoded, because the value is a deployment decision and the mechanism is not.
Narrowest-first, with a scope incrementing only when it passes. Both accounting tests were verified to fail against global-first.
Budget is consumed before the call and on every outcome; only the REFUSING scope releases its own increment.
fire_ceiling_alert on the global scope only. The sub-ceilings deliberately do not alert: they fire constantly once there are users, which trains the operator to ignore this one.
Append-only with a closed five-value enum, asserted both ways.
NO FREE-FORM FIELD EXISTS: the only string columns are event and correlation_id, asserted structurally rather than by review.
A correlation id per request, generated in middleware so rows written before any handler still carry it.
Every secret from the environment, with a raise rather than a default when unset -- a default would make every digest reproducible by anyone reading the source.
error_message is never logged. Verified against an injected debug log that leaked the API key.
The https assertion raises in the CONSTRUCTOR, so a misconfigured deployment fails at startup rather than shipping the first OTP in cleartext.
HMAC rather than a work-factor hash, following the measurement that reversed this design.
token_hash only, through the same chokepoint as the OTP.
The request body is never logged; it carries the number and the code together. Asserted by searching captured log records for both.
B1's inherited money-column assertion, discharged. VACUOUS here (stated as its own test) and verified to fire on double precision and an unconstrained numeric created by hand-written SQL.
Counter rows rather than a dict.
The count is compared AFTER the atomic increment.
One session per request, opened in middleware; the endpoint commits.
pool_pre_ping with no in-request retry: a 2 GB instance under connection pressure gets worse, not better, if every request retries.
Byte-identical responses asserted at the HTTP boundary, including content-length.
The equivalent write, rolled back inside a savepoint. Verified against both defect shapes.
Family invalidation. Verified: against an implementation invalidating only the presented token, exactly one of five transitions fails.
Enforced 15-minute expiry compared against our own clock, and no role or lens claim -- asserted by reading the full claim set.
A timeout is UNKNOWN with no retry at any layer.
The table split, asserted in both directions so neither column can migrate to the other table.
The policy keyed on the session account, set TRANSACTION-local so a pooled connection cannot leak it to the next request.
The meta-test runs first. Verified: with a correct policy and a superuser connection, a teacher reads the profile anyway.
No SMS read permission. The allowlist is empty at this Bolt, stated as a number so a first permission is a diff against zero.

reverse.target: tests/gates/test_coverage_scope.py — no upstream rule. B2's explicit --cov list did not mention B3's five new packages, so the 80% floor passed at 95% while measuring NONE of this Bolt's code. It did not fail; it silently covered less. The list is now asserted against the packages on disk in both directions, and the omission was reproduced to confirm the gate fires.

android/src/test/.../AuthSurfaceRulesTest.kt — a test defect found in the writing. The AD_ID check matched the manifest's explanatory COMMENT, which names AD_ID in order to forbid it. A test failing on the warning against a thing, while saying nothing about the thing, is worse than none: the obvious fix is to delete the warning.

app/gateway/bulksmsbd.py — _VALIDATION_CODES was declared and never read, which is dead configuration claiming more coverage than it has. taxonomy_for_code now exposes the full C.4.4 map, kept separate from outcome_for_code because the two answer different questions: what to record, versus whether a retry is allowed.

app/authz/rls.py — set_config(..., true) scopes the account id to the TRANSACTION. A session-scoped set is connection-scoped, and connections are pooled, so the next request would inherit the previous account's id. It looks identical in every single-request test.
app/db/seed_skeleton.py at 0% line coverage, deliberately. BR6.3 forbids application code from importing it and a test asserts none does; covering it would mean importing it.
